note: Rows mirror the shape the mechanical checkers emit ({prediction, verdict, observed, threshold, note}) with verdict PENDING. Each row carries baseline_value / primacy_value so a checker never compares against a literal that has drifted, and capable_of_varying with its evidence. THRESHOLD CONVENTION: the enforced per-task floor is max(FLOOR=0.03, NOISE_FLOOR[task]), so craft_task's enforced floor is 0.030 and NOT the 0.025 in NOISE_FLOOR. NO ROW PREDICTS BIT-IDENTITY: the serving stack is not bit-deterministic at temperature 0.0. Every no-change row is written on a distribution, a scalar, or a differing-row count.

generation_noise_band.why: The coordinator withdrew the claim that the serving stack is deterministic. Measured here from scratch, comparing tool-call (name, arguments) sequences against the baseline with server-assigned ids excluded, and asking separately whether a differing row's SCORE differs.

provable_no_op_arms.craft_task: chunk_limit (1 element per value, so the bound touches 0 of 150 rows) and serial_recognition (changes only recall()'s word_recognition trial-list presentation)
provable_no_op_arms.narrative_qa: serial_recognition only -- chunk_limit is NOT a no-op here (3.76 elements per value)
provable_no_op_arms.semantic_story_recall: serial_recognition only, for the same reason
provable_no_op_arms.digit_span_forward/reverse: serial_recognition and episodic_reset -- chunk_limit is NOT a no-op here (it cost 3 spans)

generation_noise_band.what_it_shows: Generation-level variation is real and large in PHRASING (7-200 rows per task) but its effect on the scored statistic is strongly task-dependent. On craft_task it is exactly zero twice: 19 rows of phrasing variation across the two no-op arms produced 0 rows of score change and a humanlikeness delta of 0.0000 in both. craft's 5-question 2AFC score is too coarse to register a rewording. On narrative_qa it is NOT zero: the one provable no-op arm changed 29 of 50 row scores and moved mean accuracy -0.0200, though its humanlikeness still moved only -0.0034. So craft_task's scored delta is the most robust of the three gist cells and narrative_qa's is the least characterised -- which is why this candidate predicts a recovery on craft and declines to predict on narrative.
generation_noise_band.correction_to_the_coordinator: The brief's follow-up cites episodic_reset as 'a no-op arm [that] moved craft -0.0280'. episodic_reset is not a no-op on craft_task. craft routes encode() through step(), which is the surface episodic_reset rewrites, and the WORKLOG already records that its claim of leaving the six encode()->recall() tasks untouched was 'empirically wrong'. Measured: its 24 differing craft rows include 18 whose score differs, all 18 inside the overflow group, and its craft accuracy delta is +0.0240 in the same direction as displacement's +0.0240 and primacy's +0.0387 -- its craft score distribution is byte-identical to displacement's {0.8:32, 1.0:118}. So -0.0280 is a mechanism effect, not a noise measurement, and craft's empirical no-op band is 0.0000 and 0.0000 rather than -0.0280.
generation_noise_band.attribution_that_replaces_bit_identity: Every craft score change, in every one of the five candidate arms, falls inside the 50 rows that write more than MAX_KEYS distinct keys: chunk_limit 0 in / 0 out, serial_recognition 0 / 0, displacement 18 / 0, episodic_reset 18 / 0, primacy 29 / 0. And the 100 craft rows that cannot overflow score exactly 1.0000 in all six runs. So craft's movement is localised to the rows where the overflow rule acts, without needing any determinism premise.
generation_noise_band.requested_from_a_repeat_baseline_run: If a repeat baseline is run, the quantity worth having is narrative_qa's per-row score agreement and the resulting humanlikeness delta between two identical configurations -- it is the only cell in the search set whose scored statistic this analysis cannot bound, and it is the cell on which three of four iteration-2 candidates were charged a floor violation. Second priority: the craft_task 5-rule-trial accuracy (50 rows), to confirm that the 0.0000/0.0000 no-op band is not a two-observation accident.

offline_replay.what: The write/delete sequences logged in the primacy run, replayed through the real PrimacyMemory and PrimacyV2Memory classes offline (no GPU, no API).
offline_replay.fidelity: PrimacyMemory reproduces primacy's own observed final_kv on 830/830 replayed rows, key AND value, across craft_task, narrative_qa, semantic_story_recall, word_recognition and both digit spans. The replay is therefore validated before any v2 figure is quoted.
offline_replay.batch_reconstruction: The dispatch log is flat, so assistant-message boundaries are reconstructed as maximal runs of consecutive write_memory calls, with a delete_key starting a new message. Licensed by measurement: 67 of 200 baseline story rows and 24 of 50 baseline word-recognition rows carry consecutive refusals at writes 5 AND 6 with no intervening delete_key, so the agent issued the second doomed write without having seen the first refusal.
offline_replay.caveat: Replaying primacy's sequences through v2 is counterfactual for the agent's own behaviour: the number of chunks written is endogenous (baseline story B=6 in 67/200 rows, primacy in 134/200), and v2's tool result names two lost keys instead of one. Retention figures from the replay are a mechanism demonstration, not a score prediction.

predictions.note: This is the arithmetic P1 depends on, separated so a P1 failure can be attributed. THE KV CLAUSE IS THE SHARP HALF; THE ACCURACY CLAUSE IS THE RISKY HALF, and the bar is deliberately set at primacy's own 0.916 rather than at displacement's 0.872. Reason: the observed craft ordering shows that retaining both ENDS beats retaining a contiguous block ({1,2,4,5} -> 0.916 against {2,3,4,5} -> 0.872), and v2's {1,2,5} retains both ends, so it can plausibly land anywhere in 0.80-0.90. The baseline's 3-key 0.800 is a different 3-key set with neither end ({2,3,4}), so it is not a safe lower bound for {1,2,5}. Setting the bar at 0.872 would have made this row likely to FAIL for a reason unrelated to the mechanism, which is exactly the miscalibration iteration 1 was criticised for. What the row still tests: three keys must not outscore four.

predictions.note: WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED, stated in advance. Offline replay: 0 of 50 narrative rows change their retained keyset under v2 -- narrative's overflowing rows are 6-write batches, where v2 and primacy lose the same keys. And the mechanism that would fix narrative is opposed to P3. The observed ordering at fixed batch size B=6 is: retain {1,2,3,4} -> 0.7875 (baseline), retain {3,4,5,6} -> 0.7647 (displacement), retain {1,2,5,6} -> 0.700 (primacy). Narrative QA tracks retained ADJACENT PAIRS (3, 3, 2), i.e. an unbroken run of the plot, while P3's both-ends retention necessarily breaks the run. The two cannot be co-satisfied by any retention rule, so this candidate keeps P3 and declares narrative_qa open. Contract observation for the record: all four iteration-2 candidates, on four unrelated surfaces, landed narrative_qa between -0.0089 and -0.0310 against an enforced floor of 0.030, and primacy's -0.0309 is 2.06 bootstrap SE and exceeds the floor by 0.0009. DISCONFIRMED OUTSIDE THE BAND in either direction: that would mean the two-key displacement message changed the agent's chunking, which is the one channel v2 opens on this task.

It is strictly more sensitive than a scored delta and strictly weaker than bit-identity: it allows phrasing to vary freely and only asks that the score not move where the mechanism cannot reach.
